1A NO: 1 OF 2024 Petition under Section 151 CPC praying that in the circumstances stated in the affidavit filed in support of the writ petition, the High Court may be pleased to direct the respondents to issue appropriate proceedings to the subordinate authorities including police not to book any cases/not to interfere with the business of the petitioner pertaining to tobacco products,
pending disposal of WP No.10501 of 2021, on the file of the High Court.

The Court made the following: ORDER "Notice before admission.
The State authorities had issued notification No.1508/FSSA/AP2015-20, dated 05.01.2021 essentially curtailing the sale and distribution of Tobacco, Panmasaia etc.
The notification is valid up to 08.01.2021.

In the meanwhile, various dealers who were dealing with these products, approached this Court on the ground that the issuance of such notification was contrary fo the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Godawat Pan Masala 1.P Limited Vs Union of india(2004 (7) SCC 68).

sentences.text: The learned Government Pleader for Medical and Health submits that the issued notification has expired and the Food Commissioner has already issued a circular directing the authorities not to interfere with the business of the dealers who are dealing with the products covered under the said notification,

The learned Government Pleader further submits that even though the notification has expired, the Government is intent on pursuing the writ petitions order to obtain a clear exposition of law on this issue.
He submits that there is batch of writ petitions in relation to this issue pending before the Division Bench.
These Writ petitions are W.P.No.3819 of 2019 and batch.
In view of the same, this Writ Petition may also be tagged along with W.P.No.3819 of 2019 and batch.
tis also recorded that the impugned notification has expired on 08.01.2021 and the authorities cannot take any action under the said notification.
It is further observed that in view of the circular issued by Food Commissioner, Andhra Pradesh Authorities shall not interfere with the business of the petitioner."
